title: Quentin and the Gravity Anew
premise: Jonah Amberdale, a terraformer and freight pilot working the contested orbits of the Meridian Belt, discovers a ship that never flew listed on her own manifest—registered to a name she buried fifteen years ago: her mother's. The ghost entry is a beacon from the Halcyon relay at the edge of dead space, where an inheritance of terraforming patents—and the political power they carry—is being claimed in her name by a syndicate that corrupted her family's legacy into a weapon of orbital extortion. Racing a countdown signal across dead space, Jonah must choose between destroying the inheritance that could redeem her name and using its power herself, while falling for Idris Vane, the syndicate defector sent to stop her. In the end she broadcasts the patents open-source to every colony, dissolving the empire her mother built, and chooses love and anonymity over the throne she was born to.
about_author: Rafael Delacroix is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent a decade writing shipping manifests before turning them into fiction. They live off-grid in the Azores, where they grow heirloom tomatoes and insist the future will belong to gardeners, not generals.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Hauling seed-stock through contested orbits, she audits her cargo logs and finds a vessel registered under her mother's name—a woman dead fifteen years—on a flight that never happened. The emotional beat is quiet dread: the invisible life she built has a crack running through it.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Flashback woven into present-day POV as Jonah tends the orbital greenhouse meant for colonists not yet born. We learn how she erased her identity after her mother's death, and why. Emotional beat: grief fossilized into routine, disturbed for the first time.

chapters.title: A Name on the Relay
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She traces the ghost entry to the Halcyon relay at the edge of dead space and receives a fragmentary signal: a countdown, and her childhood nickname no one living should know. Emotional beat: terror braided with longing—the past calling her home.

chapters.title: The Syndicate's Ledger
chapters.summary: Idris Vane's POV, introduced mid-mission. A defector inside the Corvane Syndicate, he discovers the patents behind their orbital extortion are legally tied to 'J. Amberdale'—and that his employers have dispatched hunters to collect or kill the heir. Emotional beat: complicity curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Cargo for the Dead
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She loads her freighter for a run she tells no one about, bribing a dockmaster and lying to her crew of one, an aging AI called Wren. Emotional beat: the exhilaration and guilt of choosing the dangerous road.

chapters.title: Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Jonah's ship is boarded by Syndicate inspectors; Idris, embedded in the inspection team, recognizes her name and quietly waves her through, flagging himself to his handlers. Emotional beat: two strangers gambling everything on each other without yet meeting.

chapters.title: What Mother Built
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, drifting through the belt's outer stations. She uncovers what the Amberdale patents actually do: atmospheric processors repurposed to hold colonies' air supply hostage. Emotional beat: horror—inheriting not a legacy but a weapon.

chapters.title: The Defector's Price
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. His betrayal discovered, he burns his cover and steals a skiff, transmitting coordinates to Jonah with a warning: the Syndicate has activated the relay's dead-man switch. Emotional beat: liberation and terror in the same breath.

chapters.title: Dead Space
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Beyond the last beacon, her ship runs silent through a region where signals go to die; Wren begins failing, and Jonah confronts the void both literal and personal. Emotional beat: isolation pressing down, resolve hardening like scar tissue.

chapters.title: Rendezvous at Halcyon
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Jonah and Idris dock at the derelict relay; their first meeting is at gunpoint, each mistaking the other for a hunter. Trust is negotiated in bullets and breath. Emotional beat: wary electricity—the first spark of something neither can afford.

chapters.title: The Countdown Room
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Inside the relay core they find her mother's final message: a confession that she built the Syndicate's chokehold knowingly, and left the patents to Jonah hoping she'd destroy them. Emotional beat: fury and forgiveness colliding over a dead woman's voice.

chapters.title: Hunters in the Dark
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Syndicate strike teams board the relay; he and Jonah fight through maintenance shafts, and he takes a wound shielding her. Emotional beat: duty inverted—he now serves her cause, not his orders.

chapters.title: Love Against the Clock
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. While Idris recovers, they plan the broadcast that would free the patents to every colony—and admit, almost accidentally, what they mean to each other. Emotional beat: tenderness stolen from catastrophe, all the more precious for it.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The Syndicate matriarch, Sera Corvane, hails the relay personally: keep the patents, take your mother's throne, and the colonies stay leveraged but alive. Power offered like a gift. Emotional beat: temptation wearing the face of legitimacy.

chapters.title: Throne of Air
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She walks the Syndicate flagship under truce and sees the empire up close—comfortable, orderly, monstrous. Corvane argues corruption is just inheritance managed well. Emotional beat: doubt's sharpest hour; the devil makes excellent sense.

chapters.title: Wren's Last Flight
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Her failing AI sacrifices itself to jam the Syndicate's counter-signal, buying hours and dying with a joke on its lips. Emotional beat: devastating loss that clarifies everything worth saving.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax, dual POV. From the Halcyon core, Jonah releases the patents open-source to every colony in the belt as Syndicate forces breach the relay; Idris holds the line so the transmission completes. Emotional beat: triumph purchased with blood, irreversible and bright.

chapters.title: Aftermath of an Empire
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. The Syndicate fractures as colonies seize their own atmosphere processors; Corvane's fall is quiet, administrative, total. Emotional beat: the strange anticlimax of watching tyranny die by paperwork.

chapters.title: Inheritance Refused
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Offered leadership of the liberated colonies, she declines publicly, reading her mother's confession aloud so the name Amberdale means release, not rule. Emotional beat: laying a fifteen-year burden down in front of witnesses.

chapters.title: What the Garden Grows
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She returns to the orbital greenhouse and plants the first seeds for colonists who will arrive knowing clean air as a birthright, not a ransom. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope—the gardener's faith in futures unseen.

chapters.title: Two Names, No Throne
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Jonah and Idris register a small freighter under new names, choosing each other and obscurity over power. Emotional beat: love as the final act of freedom, chosen daily rather than declared once.

chapters.title: Gravity Anew
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Jonah's POV. Years later, hauling honest cargo, she passes the Halcyon relay—now a public archive—and lets its light wash over the hull. Emotional beat: peace; the pull that once dragged her toward the past now gently holds her in the present.
